thought_title: Union with the bishop at the one altar

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἐν μικρῷ χρόνῳ τοιαύτην συνήθειαν ἔσχον πρὸς τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ὑμῶν, οὐκ ἀνθρωπίνην οὖσαν, ἀλλὰ πνευματικήν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς μακαρίζω τοὺς ἐγκεκραμένους οὕτως, ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, καὶ ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρί, ἵνα πάντα ἐν ἑνότητι σύμφωνα ᾖ; [2] μηδεὶς πλανάσθω: ἑὰν μή τις ᾖ ἐντὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, ὑστερεῖται τοῦ ἄρτου τοῦ θεοῦ. εἰ γὰρ ἑνὸς καὶ δευτέρου προσευχὴ τοσαύτην ἰσχὺν ἔχει, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ἥ τε τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ πάσης τῆς ἐκκλησίας; [3] ὁ οὖν μὴ ἐρχόμενος ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὗτος ἤδη ὑπερηφανεῖ καὶ ἑαυτὸν διέκρινεν. γέγραπται γάρ: Ὑπερηφάνοις ὁ θεὸς ἀντιτάσσεται, σπουδάσωμεν οὖν μὴ ἀντιτάσσεσθαι τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, ἵνα ὦμεν θεῷ ὑποτασσόμενοι.
pass_a_gloss: For if I in a short time came to such intimacy with your bishop, an intimacy not human but spiritual, how much more do I count you blessed who are blended with him in this way, as the church is with Jesus Christ and as Jesus Christ is with the Father, so that all things may be in harmony in unity? Let no one be deceived: unless someone is inside the altar, he lacks the bread of God. For if the prayer of one or two has such strength, how much more the prayer of the bishop and of the whole church? So whoever does not come to the common gathering is already proud and has separated himself in judgment. For it is written, God opposes the proud. Let us be eager, then, not to oppose the bishop, so that we may be subject to God.

lemmas.gloss: altar; the place of the altar
to the same place; together in assembly

pass_b_english: In a short time I came to know your bishop with a closeness that was not human but spiritual. If that is true of me, how much more do I count you blessed, who are joined with him as the church is joined with Jesus Christ, and as Jesus Christ is joined with the Father, so that all things may sound together in unity?

Let no one be deceived. Anyone who is not within the altar goes without the bread of God. For if the prayer of one or two carries such power, how much more the prayer of the bishop and the whole church?

So whoever stays away from the assembly is already proud and has passed sentence on himself. For it is written, "God opposes the proud" (Proverbs 3:34; James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5). Let us be eager, then, not to oppose the bishop, so that we may be subject to God.

choices.why: Ignatius's own spatial phrase: inside the altar's precinct, the eucharistic assembly. Kept literal because it is striking and theological.
ἐγκεράννυμι is to blend or mix closely; 'joined' keeps the closeness without a chemistry image.
διακρίνω can mean to separate or to judge; staying away both sets him apart and judges him. 'Passed sentence' keeps the judicial edge.
Keeps Ignatius's wordplay: God opposes the proud, so do not oppose the bishop; be subject to God.
rejected: resists ... set ourselves in opposition (ANF; breaks the echo)

anf_compare.notes: Sense aligned. ANF 'condemned himself' is one side of διέκρινεν (separate / judge). ANF 'that so all things may agree' keeps the purpose clause; we render it as an exclamation following the rhetorical question.

bible_refs.note: LXX κύριος ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται; introduced by γέγραπται
ὁ θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται: Ignatius has the same words with ὁ θεός

notes: Whole chapter 5 (sections 1-3) matches the ANF span.
ANF marks Matthew 18:19 for 'the prayer of one or two'; Matthew has 'two of you'. Kept as a possible allusion only, not inline.
Possible echo of Ephesians 5:24 (the church subject to Christ) in 'as the church is with Jesus Christ'; not inline.

checker_dispute: checker b objects to the inline (Proverbs 3:34; James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5). Ignatius introduces a real quotation with γέγραπται γάρ: Ὑπερηφάνοις ὁ θεὸς ἀντιτάσσεται, which is word for word James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 (ὁ θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται), from Proverbs 3:34 LXX (κύριος ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται).

review.notes: Paragraph [1] matches Ignatius, Ephesians 5.1–3. Εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἐν μικρῷ χρόνῳ τοιαύτην συνήθειαν ἔσχον πρὸς τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ὑμῶν, οὐκ ἀνθρωπίνην οὖσαν, ἀλλὰ πνευματικήν is kept in A as “For if I in a short time came to such intimacy with your bishop, an intimacy not human but spiritual” and in B as a real conditional restated by “If that is true of me”; τοὺς ἐγκεκραμένους οὕτως, ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, καὶ ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρί, ἵνα πάντα ἐν ἑνότητι σύμφωνα ᾖ is “blended with him… in harmony in unity” / “joined with him… sound together in unity.” ἑὰν μή τις ᾖ ἐντὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, ὑστερεῖται τοῦ ἄρτου τοῦ θεοῦ and ἑνὸς καὶ δευτέρου προσευχή stay “inside/within the altar,” “lacks/goes without the bread of God,” and “prayer of one or two.” ὁ μὴ ἐρχόμενος ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ… ὑπερηφανεῖ καὶ ἑαυτὸν διέκρινεν keeps the non-attender as agent; A “separated himself in judgment” and B “passed sentence on himself” are compatible senses of διέκρινεν, not a reversal. γέγραπται γάρ: Ὑπερηφάνοις ὁ θεὸς ἀντιτάσσεται is “God opposes the proud,” with B’s required inline (Proverbs 3:34; James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5) not shown false by the locked text; σπουδάσωμεν… μὴ ἀντιτάσσεσθαι τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, ἵνα ὦμεν θεῷ ὑποτασσόμενοι is “not to oppose the bishop, so that we may be subject to God.” Title names the union-and-altar thought.

Source identity confirmed: Ignatius Ephesians 5, Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text. Completeness: All three clauses of the single paragraph are present in both Pass A and B with no omissions; repetitions, qualifications, and quotations preserved. Negation: 'μηδεὶς πλανάσθω' rendered as 'Let no one be deceived' in both Pass A and B. Agency: Clear attribution of actions (I came to intimacy, you are blessed, God opposes the proud, we must not oppose the bishop). Modality: Possibility/necessity in 'πόσῳ μᾶλλον' (how much more) preserved in both. Doctrine: Unity of bishop, church, Christ, Father maintained; eucharistic altar imagery intact. Scripture: γέγραπται γάρ: Ὑπερηφάνοις ὁ θεὸς ἀντιτάσσεται correctly identified as James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 (and Proverbs 3:34 LXX) in Pass B and notes; inline citation added per rule. Title: 'Union with the bishop at the one altar' names the theological thought, not just locus. Notes disclose OCR damage uncertain? None noted; variants empty; Bible references explained. Pass A fidelity: Every clause's sense preserved (e.g., 'ἐγκεκραμένους' as 'blended', 'ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό' as 'common gathering'). Pass B: No addition or contradiction; 'passed sentence on himself' for 'ἑαυτὸν διέκρινεν' is a valid judicial nuance per lemmas. All checks passed.
